role: Local runner (make ci-local / ci-local-unit) that parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and executes its `run:` steps in order with job+step env, feeding $GITHUB_OUTPUT values to later steps.
toplevel: set -uo pipefail. Args: --scope X (default gates; no validation), --list; unknown -> exit 2. Exit 2 if ci.yml absent (must be run from repo root). Sources preflight and calls gate_require_unmutated_tree. Python (needs PyYAML): job_runs() evaluates each job's `if:` against the scope as GitHub evaluates it against the dispatch input: no `if:` -> runs; `inputs.X == 'v'` / `inputs.X != 'v'` (optionally wrapped in ${{ }}) compared with INPUT_DEFAULTS (scope = --scope, baseline-ref ''); any other condition -> sys.exit with an error naming the job. With ci.yml today: gates runs lint-and-budgets and strict-concurrency; unit and full also run thread-sanitizer and tests. Steps with `uses:` or no `run:` are dropped silently; step-level `if:` is ignored. expand() resolves ${{ steps.X.outputs.Y }}, ${{ inputs.X }}, and the `inputs.X == 'v' && 'a' || 'b'` ternary; any other expression becomes ''. --list prints RUN/SKIP per step and exits 0. Otherwise warns when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, then for each step: CANNOT_RUN_LOCALLY regex (sudo xcode-select; brew install/update/tap; a run block writing $GITHUB_PATH, i.e. the SwiftLint install; actions/...) -> SKIP; else `bash -lc <expanded run>` with merged env and temp GITHUB_OUTPUT/ENV/STEP_SUMMARY; step outputs parsed when the step has an id; temp .ghout unlinked (the .env and .summary files are never removed). Prints failures with last 12 output lines; exit 1 if any failed; at scope gates notes that the test and Thread Sanitizer jobs did not run. Only ci.yml is simulated; gates.yml (the push-triggered workflow) is not. Units named `fn print` are Python `print()` calls misidentified as shell functions.

units.does: Not a function: a Python `print()` inside the heredoc (blank line before the summary) misidentified as a shell function `print`. Always executed after the step loop.
units.entry: executed inline by the heredoc python

units.does: Not a function: a Python `print()` inside the heredoc emitting a blank line after each failed step's output tail; misidentified as a shell function `print`.
units.entry: executed inline in the `for name, cmd, proc in failed` loop of the heredoc python
